title: Pouch steps sheet
subject: Art & Design
unit: Summer 1: Urban landscapes and a felt pouch (Street Detectives)
source: Written for art/y2 lesson 11 (Pouch steps sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 11: Cut, stitch and join: a felt pouch. Listen, look, then do the tasks with a grown-up.

timeline.text: Thread the needle and tie a knot at the end (adult helps).
Put the two felt rectangles together, one on top of the other.
Running stitch down one side: up, along a little, down.
Stitch along the bottom, then up the other side.
Leave the top open. Tie a knot at the end.
Put the needle back in its pot.

panels.title: Safe sewing
points: Needle back in its pot after use

parts.text: Thread the needle and knot the end
Stitch the bottom and other side

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A pouch open at the top

keywords.def: one loop of thread through fabric
in and out in a straight line

questions.q: Show me: point to where the next stitch goes.
questions.a: A spot a little further along the line

questions.q: Why do we tie a knot?
questions.a: So the thread does not pull out

questions.q: Core: Sew two felt rectangles together on three sides with running stitch, with an adult helping.
questions.a: A pouch with stitches along three sides and the top open

questions.q: Extend: Decorate the front with a felt shape or button (adult helps).
Stretch: Say one thing that went well and one thing to improve.
questions.a: For example: even stitches; the knot came undone

questions.q: Which side do we leave open?
questions.a: A) The top. The open top lets us put things in; the other three sides are stitched.

questions.q: Big question: how do two flat pieces become a pouch?
questions.a: We join three sides with stitches and leave the top open
